title: Cabled Aran single-bed throw
subtitle: A 140 by 200 cm single-bed throw in a full Aran pattern on 5 mm needles.
excerpt: A 140 by 200 cm single-bed throw in aran weight on 5 mm needles, featuring a traditional Aran panel repeat: honeycomb cable, rope cable, double-moss filler, and seed-stitch borders. A long-term project using about 2,500 g of aran. ADVANCED: multiple simultaneous cable repeats with long row counts.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 15th series (1899), §Aran Pattern Covers, gives a full-Aran sofa cover in multiple cable panels. The honeycomb cable (C4F alternating with C4B) and rope cable (C4F every 4 rows) are documented in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), §Cable Stitches.

knitting.gaugeText: 18 sts × 24 rows = 10 × 10 cm in Aran cable pattern on 5 mm needles, blocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: An all-over cable pattern where C4F and C4B crossings alternate across the width and shift by two stitches every four rows. The result is a surface of interlocking diamonds that resembles a honeycomb. Every stitch is in a cable cross on every fourth row.
A six- or eight-stitch cable where all crossings go in the same direction (all C4F or all C4B) on every fourth row. The column spirals uniformly to the left or right, resembling a twisted rope.

content.text: A single-panel rectangle worked flat on 5 mm needles. The pattern uses four Aran panels:
honeycomb cable
rope cable
, double-moss filler, and seed-stitch borders. Finished size: 140 cm by 200 cm.

Single-panel construction; no seaming. The throw is wider and longer than a baby blanket or lap throw: 140 cm covers a single bed. The panel repeat runs as follows across 252 stitches: [seed 8] + [honeycomb 24] + [seed 4] + [rope 12] + [seed 4] + [double-moss 24] + [seed 4] + [rope 12] + [seed 4] + [honeycomb 24] + [seed 8] + adjustments for cable draw-in. Multiple cable panels operate simultaneously; the ADVANCED rating reflects the cognitive demand of tracking four different cable sequences at once over 480 rows. Budget about 2,500 g (about 4,400 m / 4,810 yards) of aran. This is a 10- to 14-skein project; buy in matched dye lots and alternate skeins.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 2,500 g (about 4,400 m / 4,810 yards) of aran-weight 100% wool or wool-blend yarn. A smooth cream or natural aran shows cable definition best.

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 5 mm (UK 6 / US 8) circular needle, 150 cm or longer (the throw is very wide)

items.name: Cable needles
items.qty: 2 (different sizes or shapes to distinguish honeycomb from rope cables mid-row)

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 8 or more (one at each panel boundary)

content.text: Gauge

18 stitches and 24 rows to 10 cm in Aran cable pattern on 5 mm needles, blocked. Aran cables draw in significantly; the unblocked throw will be about 120 cm wide. Block before measuring final dimensions.

At 18 stitches per 10 cm blocked, 140 cm requires 252 stitches. The panel arrangement above gives exactly 252 stitches. If your gauge is 16 per 10 cm, use 224 stitches and adjust the panel widths proportionally.
Stitches used

items.name: C4F
items.qty: cable 4 front: sl2 hold front, k2, k2 from cable needle

items.name: C4B
items.qty: cable 4 back: sl2 hold back, k2, k2 from cable needle

items.name: C6F
items.qty: cable 6 front: sl3 hold front, k3, k3 from cable needle

items.name: Honeycomb row (RS)
items.qty: across 24-stitch panel: *C4F, C4B; rep from * (rows 1 and 3 of repeat)

items.name: Rope row (RS)
items.qty: across 12-stitch panel: C6F, k6 (or k6, C6F)

content.text: Pattern
Cast-on
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 252 stitches. Long-tail tail: (5 × 252) / 10 + 15 = 126 + 15 = 141 cm. Measure 160 cm. Place panel boundary markers as you cast on.
Body

RS rows: work each panel section according to its pattern (seed, honeycomb, rope, or double moss), slipping panel markers. WS rows: k the knits and p the purls within each panel (cable panels purl their stitches on the WS; seed and double-moss panels maintain their texture).

Honeycomb cable rows fire every 2 rows (rows 1 and 3 of a 4-row repeat, alternating C4F/C4B and C4B/C4F). Rope cable rows fire every 4 rows. Track both independently with a dedicated row counter per cable type. When you set this aside, note the row number in each of the two cable cycles.
Stitch count check-ins

At row 240 (about 100 cm): count across all panels. You should have 252 stitches total. Recount within each panel to catch any errors before the second half. At row 478 (about 199 cm): final count before casting off.
Common faults

Honeycomb pattern losing its offset: the C4F and C4B crossings on row 3 must be shifted by 2 stitches relative to row 1 crossings. If both rows cross in the same positions, the result is vertical rope cables rather than a honeycomb grid.
Rope cable crossing on row 2 instead of row 4: the row counter for the rope panels was not tracked separately from the honeycomb counter. Use two separate counters or colour-code a paper tally.

Weight of the throw causing dropped stitches: at 2,500 g, the throw is very heavy on the needles. Use the longest available circular needle to distribute the weight in your lap; work on a surface where the throw can rest rather than hang.
Cast-off
Cast off in pattern with needles one size larger. A 252-stitch cast-off with cables benefits from pausing every 50 stitches to check the tension.
Finishing
Weave in all ends. Block with steam or by soaking: a throw this size needs a large blocking surface (two foam mats side by side) and at least 48 hours to dry fully.
Care

Hand wash in cool water for non-superwash aran; machine wash on gentle 30-degree cycle for superwash. Lay flat to dry on a clean surface. A wet Aran throw at 2,500 g is very heavy; support it fully when lifting from the wash.
What to try next

From a traditional Aran throw, try a gansey-inspired blanket next. Use the same aran weight and needle. The panel vocabulary changes: gansey stitch patterns replace the Aran ones. The construction stays flat.
